key_insight: SwimBird enables hybrid autoregressive MLLMs to dynamically switch between visual latent ‘thoughts’ and textual chain-of-thought, preserving strong visual reasoning without degrading text-based logical reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing MLLMs either rely on text-based CoT (weak for vision-intensive tasks) or inject fixed visual latent states (which help vision but harm text reasoning); SwimBird addresses the need for a controllable, switchable reasoning mode that supports both modalities.
method: Hybrid autoregressive backbone with two reasoning paths: continuous visual-latent ‘visual thoughts’ and discrete textual CoT, accessible during generation.
A lightweight mode controller (mode tokens/gating) and mode-conditioned training to elicit and switch the appropriate reasoning process per task or prompt.
Joint training objectives and auxiliary supervision to maintain performance in each mode and reduce cross-mode interference (mode-specific losses and distillation/regularization).
impact: Practitioners get a single MLLM that can be flexibly steered toward vision-heavy or text-heavy reasoning without retraining separate models—improving robustness on mixed multimodal workloads and simplifying deployment.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing dual reasoning paths (visual-latent vs textual CoT) and a mode controller/gate.
Before/after examples: same multimodal input with visual-mode output vs text-mode output to illustrate behavior differences.
Bar chart or radar comparing vision-task vs text-reasoning performance for baseline MLLMs, fixed-visual-latent models, and SwimBird.
Flowchart of inference that shows manual (prompt) vs automatic controller switching between modes.
paper_title: SwimBird: Eliciting Switchable Reasoning Mode in Hybrid Autoregressive MLLMs
paper_authors: Jintao Tong, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Kunyu Shi
